known.title: The no-CI fallback of the shipped plan contract tells the agent to run the docks author script `node scripts/ci.mjs`.
known.summary: The checks policy (plan-contract.md:233-237) now says: 'When the repository has no configured checks, run `node scripts/ci.mjs` as the local gate, treat its green result as the check result, and say so in the merge question.' plan-contract.md is a shipped reference of the plan-manager skill. plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/AGENTS.md:35-41 governs it: 'Shipped skill bodies (SKILL.md + `references/`) and the shipped agent body are consumer-facing - never name docks plugin-author scripts (`scripts/ci.mjs`, `scripts/skills/*`, ...) as a step. Make verification self-contained or refer generically to "the project's CI / validators, if present".' The new sentence names `scripts/ci.mjs` as a step. A consumer repository has no such file. So in a consumer repository without checks, plan-manager runs a missing command before the merge question. The plan decision says only 'treat the green local gate as the check result'. Check at head+patch: `node scripts/skills/no-author-scripts.mjs plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills plugins/plan-lifecycle/agents` exits 1 and prints 'FAIL: plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md:235'. This guard runs in the plugin gate, so acceptance A5 also fails.

known.title: The diff changes the text of the unknown-heading refusal, but the contract still lists the old exact string.
known.summary: sectionMap() now fails with 'unknown section heading: <title>; use only <sections>, or demote it to ### inside an existing section' (plan.mjs:374). The test at scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs:607 expects the new text. plan-contract.md:196 says 'Refusals exit 1. These stderr strings are exact, with angle brackets replaced:'. plan-contract.md:216 still lists 'unknown section heading: <title>; use only <the seven sections> or write it below an existing section as ### or plain text'. The diff does not change line 216. Scenario: `edit` of a body with a `## Context` section prints the new string on stderr. That string does not match the string of the contract. An agent or a script that matches the documented refusal does not recognize it. The plan keeps this refusal for a full body and does not ask for a new text.

known.title: The severity field regex makes the brackets and the colon optional, so a line that starts with the word High or Critical turns a code pass into fixes-required.
known.summary:
parseReviewComment() (plan.mjs:539) tests each line with /^\s*(?:[-*]\s+)?\[?(?:critical|high)\]?:?/i. Both brackets and the colon are optional, and no boundary follows the word. So the regex accepts a bare severity word at the line start, a half bracket such as '[high', and words such as 'Highlights' or 'High-level'. plan-contract.md:145-147 says: 'A code pass derives as fixes-required when any finding line starts with a `critical` or `high` severity field, written `- [high]` or `high:`, in any case. Severity words inside finding prose do not count.' The plan decision says the same. Checked with node at head+patch: parseReviewComment('### Code review round 1
Code-review: pass
- [low] src/api.mjs:3 - rename the helper
Highlights: the parser change is sound.') and parseReviewComment('### Code review round 1
Code-review: pass
- Critical paths were checked; no defect found.') both return verdict fixes-required. The regex /^\s*(?:[-*]\s+)?(?:\[(?:critical|high)\]|(?:critical|high):)/i returns pass for both. A trusted pass then reads as fixes-required, and archive refuses with 'archive requires Code-review: pass'. The new review cases (scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs:340-347) do not catch this, because no case starts a line with a severity word without its delimiter.
